A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same AUHead research work. All 23 pages, including equations, tables, figures, references, and Appendices A–E, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments, AU-prediction ablations, benchmark comparisons, and a 25-participant user study in Section 4, plus qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results, user study, and appendix qualitative outputs.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same AU tokenization, emotion-then-AU generation, AU-conditioned diffusion components, training objectives, and inference guidance.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MEAD and CREMA evaluations, the unseen-audio/identity and visual-style examples in Figure 7, and the emotion-guided scenarios in Appendix B.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Table 3, the HalloV2 user study in Table 4, and the main-text and appendix qualitative comparisons.

E3.justification: The splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, and training settings in Section 4.1 are unchanged. The user study retains its blind comparison of 32 clips rated by 25 participants.

E4.justification: The generation-order ablation in Table 1, AU-representation ablation in Table 2, guidance-scale analysis in Figure 3, and qualitative/generalization case studies are identical.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates and preference percentages. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are retained unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports AUHead (MEMO) FID values of 10.9671 on MEAD and 8.2361 on CREMA in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6) and their mathematical definitions are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about ALM-based AU generation, interpretable expression control, and talking-head generation performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications remain identical, including the expression-control/visual-quality trade-off, possible synchronization mismatches, ALM context limitations, and future extension to in-the-wild conditions.

D1.justification: Hardware, training times, hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions, repository information, AU validation details, and the Appendix C prompt template are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to prior methods are unchanged; text merely flows differently across pages 2–3.

P1.justification: v2 adds Hanyu Jiang's affiliation with the State Key Laboratory of Communication Content Cognition, People's Daily Online, adjusts author punctuation, and rearranges contact information. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded affiliation block shifts the abstract, Figure 1, and text across pages 1–3, alongside the updated arXiv version stamp. Figure/table content is unchanged; pages 4–23 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 updates affiliation information and causes minor front-page reflow. The scientific content, supporting evidence, reproducibility information, and appendices are unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
